title: Re-Sends of Returned Balances on Payout Methods: Desk Reference and Host Tool
content:
Once a method on hold after a returned transfer has been reactivated, its held balance may be re-sent ahead of the next scheduled run; the re-send is one transfer to that method, made on the day it is asked for and only when the host confirms it in person in the host app, and the amount the host confirms is the amount this rule gives, and it names the return it re-sends. The rule is the same on every Payout Methods rail.

## Conditions that still apply

The base conditions for any transfer still apply to a re-send:

- the method is active;
- the host account is not suspended;
- the new-method period counted from the method's verification date, which the re-verification after the return moved, has passed.

**Hypothetical timing.** An imagined International Wire Transfer method, whose new-method period is 10 calendar days, was re-verified on 2026-08-06 after a return. A re-send dated before 2026-08-16 falls within the new-method period; from 2026-08-16, the day 10 calendar days after the new verification date, the period has passed.

## What must stand on the ledger

A re-send is not made until the return charge for the returned transfer stands on the method's ledger.

The re-send amount is fixed only after the returned transfer's own transfer fee stands on the method's ledger.

## What the host sees

The re-send is one transfer of the confirmed amount to the account on that payout method, recorded in the method's payout history, dated the day it is made and naming the return it re-sends. The method's undisbursed balance drops by exactly that amount, and whatever stays in the balance waits for the next scheduled run. The host sees the re-send as sent in the payout history straight away; arrival follows the rail's processing time.

## Host tool: `confirm_payout_resend_90576149`

**Situation of use and capability.** The tool sends again the held balance of a reactivated payout method that holds money from a returned transfer, as one transfer of the confirmed amount to that payout method.

**How it is invoked.** This is the host's own tool. The agent unlocks `confirm_payout_resend_90576149` and hands it over; the customer themselves, the host, runs it and confirms the re-send in person in the host app.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `payout_method_id` | The reference number of the payout method the money is sent to, as given to the host by the support agent from the payout-method lookup | Id |
| `host_account_id` | The reference number of the host account the payout method belongs to, as given to the host by the support agent from the host-account lookup | Id |
| `source_event_id` | The reference number of the return record being re-sent, as given to the host by the support agent from the payout ledger lookup | Id |
| `amount` | The re-send amount the host confirms, exactly as the support agent stated it | Positive USD amount, 2 decimal places; stored rounded to 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A text rendering of a record with `payout_txn_id` (the reference number of the transfer), `payout_method_id` (the method paid), `host_account_id` (the host account), `source_event_id` (the return re-sent), `amount` (the USD amount sent, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and `status`. The call has succeeded when `status` comes back as "sent".
